literal: Friendship that weighs the gain, those who take what is received, and thieves, are equal.
translation: A friendship that calculates only personal gain, those who associate with others only for payment, and thieves are all alike.
modern: கிடைக்கும் லாபத்தை ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்கும் நட்பும், கைம்மாறு பெறுபவர்களும், திருடர்களும் சமமானவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares three types of people: a calculating friend who only values a relationship for what they can gain from it, those who offer companionship solely for material payment, and thieves. All three are driven purely by selfish motives and lack genuine affection or moral commitment. The poet warns that a friend who constantly weighs their profit is no better than a thief, as both seek to take from you without any real bond. Understanding this comparison helps us identify and avoid superficial, transactional relationships.
